answer:
Based on the American Diabetes Association (ADA) guidelines, SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended for patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease (CKD) when their estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is at least 20 mL/min/1.73m². These recommendations aim to reduce the progression of CKD and cardiovascular risk.

Please note this recommendation applies to type 2 diabetic patients with CKD, regardless of whether they have albuminuria or hypertension. SGLT2 inhibitors are also part of the recommended class for slowing CKD progression in all stages when combined with ACE inhibitors (also known as angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors) or ARBs (angiotensin receptor blockers), especially in patients presenting with albuminuria and hypertension. 

For more detailed information, you should consult the guidelines published by the American Diabetes Association [ADA Standard of Care in Diabetes, 2024].
